title: Beth · Armidale
name: Beth
story:
## About me
I am an international student studying at the university of New England.

## Our community and the ocean
The ocean is like a second home. It brings others together when you go on adventures to the ocean. It’s a main factor to our eco system as it’s a source life that covers about 71% of our earth. And has built many connections with other which ties into their culture, such as Torres  Strait Islander’s, Māori, Tongan and many others who also live in Australia have many stories and meanings that connect with the ocean.

## An issue we see
Over pollution and environmental damage to coral reefs. Whether that is from rubbish floating into the ocean or to coral dying due climate change and frequent marine heat waves.

## What we're doing
I am personally not involved with anything regarding a club or team who find the ocean important but in my community as we live a couple hours away from the coast, it brings a special intentionality when the ocean is talked about.

## What I wish the world understood
I wish they could understand how little we actually know the waters of our own planet. At times it feels like they spend more time trying to get off it. The ocean is the only one we have, so why aren’t we fighting for it and protecting it more.

## Biggest issues here
Plastic pollution, Coral reef damage, Rising ocean temperatures & stronger climate change, Agriculture, industrial & chemical pollution

title: Tamatoa · Lyon
name: Tamatoa
story:
## About me
I work as a Management Controller for a logistics company. I enjoy fishing or simply relaxing by the beach.

## Our community and the ocean
The ocean is for my community a source of revenue, food and entertainment. It is central to our lives. In the marquesas islands, pollution and overfishing hasn’t gone out of control yet and we can still have access to an abundance of fishes to provide for our families.

## An issue we see
The rising of pollution in the lagoons. The lack of appropriate waste management infrastructure is impacting the earth and with the rain the lagoons directly.

## What we're doing
Growing up in the Marquesas Islands, I learned that the ocean is not just a resource but part of our identity, culture, and way of life. We can protect it by strengthening traditional Polynesian knowledge, educating younger generations, and supporting locally managed marine areas that allow fish populations and marine ecosystems to recover.

## What I wish the world understood
I wish people understood that in Polynesia, the ocean is not a barrier separating islands but a source of life that connects our people, our ancestors, and our future. Conservation efforts should listen to local communities and respect our ancestral knowledge, because the people who live closest to the ocean often have some of the deepest connections to protecting it.

## Biggest issues here
Plastic pollution, Decline of marine wildlife & biodiversity, Coral reef damage

title: Thais · Vitória
name: Thais
story:
## About me
Digital Marketing Specialist, I enjoy going to the beach on weekends and spending time by the ocean.

## Our community and the ocean
In my community in Espírito Santo, Brazil, the ocean is a place where people relax, spend time with family and friends, and enjoy nature, especially on weekends. We also have marine conservation areas and initiatives that help protect ocean wildlife, reminding us how important it is to preserve marine life for future generations.

## An issue we see
One ocean issue I see in my community is the amount of trash people leave on the beaches, especially after weekends and holidays. This pollution harms marine life and makes it important for people to be more responsible and respectful of the environment.

## What we're doing
My community could do more to protect the ocean by enforcing stricter laws against littering, raising public awareness about beach pollution, and providing more support for marine conservation projects. I believe education and community involvement are essential to protecting marine life and keeping our beaches clean.

## What I wish the world understood
I wish people around the world understood how important the ocean is to our community, not only as a place for leisure and relaxation but also as a part of our daily lives and our connection with nature. I believe organizations should invest more in educating people and supporting local marine conservation efforts to protect the ocean for future generations.

## Biggest issues here
Plastic pollution, Water pollution, Lack of government regulation/implementation of sustainable laws

title: Tanya · Douglas
name: Tanya
story:
## About me
I live on the Isle of Man and work as a Maritime Security Supervisor at the Sea Terminal in Douglas, so the sea is part of my everyday working life. I enjoy coastal walks, taking in the beautiful scenery and spending time by the sea with my family.

## Our community and the ocean
Living on the Isle of Man, the sea connects our community to the world, with ferries bringing passengers, visitors and essential supplies to the island. In my work at the Sea Terminal, I see how much we depend on these connections and how rough weather can disrupt everyday plans. For me, the coast is also a place to relax and enjoy time with family, and it is a special part of what makes the island home.

## An issue we see
One issue I notice is litter and plastic washed up along our beaches and coastline. It spoils these beautiful places, and I worry about the harm it can cause to marine wildlife.

## What we're doing
Our community could encourage more regular beach cleans and involve local schools, families and businesses. Reducing single-use plastics and providing well-maintained bins near beaches would also help, alongside teaching children why caring for the sea matters

## What I wish the world understood
I wish people understood how much a small island community depends on the sea for everyday supplies, work and keeping in touch with family and friends. Protecting it means protecting our home and our children’s future. I would like organisations to support practical local efforts while also tackling pollution before it reaches our shores.

## Biggest issues here
Plastic pollution, Water pollution, Sea level rise & coastal erosion

title: Eritai · Banraeaba
name: Eritai
story:
## About me
Managing Director, I love fishing on the weekends

## Our community and the ocean
The ocean is our life, identity, and culture, providing food, transportation, and livelihoods while connecting our families and communities across the islands of Kiribati. It represents our strength and resilience, and we have a responsibility to protect it for future generations, especially from the impacts of climate change.

## An issue we see
One major ocean issue in our community is coastal erosion and rising sea levels, which threaten our homes, land and livelihoods. We are witnessing hirelings gradually disappearing and seawater flooding our communities, especially during high tides and storms.

## What we're doing
Our community can protect the ocean by reducing plastic waste, organising coastal cleanups, planting mangroves, and promoting sustainable fishing practices. We should also strengthen traditional conservation practices and educate younger generations about the importance of protecting our marine environment.

## What I wish the world understood
I wish the world understood that for the people of Kiribati, the ocean is not just our livelihood but an essential part of our identity, culture, and survival. International organization should focus more on practical, community-led solutions that address coastal erosion, marine pollution and climate change while respecting our traditional knowledge.

## Biggest issues here
Plastic pollution, Sea level rise & coastal erosion, Lack of government regulation/implementation of sustainable laws

title: Charlotte · Santa Barbara California
name: Charlotte
story:
## About me
I’m born and raised in Santa Barbara CA USA and one thing I’m concerned about is ocean warming and global warming as a whole. Ocean warming to my knowledge can confuse and force animals out of their natural habitats in order for them to try to find a place that actually fits for them creating a disturbance in the life cycle.

## Our community and the ocean
My city has a really close connection to the beach and ocean, it’s a staple of everyone’s life who lives here. Going to the beach is most likely the #1 activity of many families and most teenagers.

## An issue we see
In my community the biggest concern I see regarding the ocean is frequent oil spills on our beaches. This not only prohibits people from enjoying the beach, but harms animals and the habitat not only in the ocean but next to the shores.

## What we're doing
When oil spills happen there is a lot of effort by professionals to clean it up, but I think we should work harder to keep it from happening in the first place. The city also organizes beach trash pick ups, but either they aren’t frequent or they aren’t advertised well because I don’t hear of them a lot.

## What I wish the world understood
I wish people really took into consideration the amount of ocean that takes up our world and it is one of the most important things that keeps our climate and experience on this earth balanced. Without it balancing things like climate, it can be used as a weapon against us.

## Biggest issues here
Plastic pollution, Water pollution, Rising ocean temperatures & stronger climate change
